raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Make the GPU's per-request logit counts decide which grammar mask rows are applied, instead of a CPU-built mask→logit mapping.

- The scheduler emits a fixed-width block of `num_spec_tokens + 1` mask rows per structured-output request.
- The MRV2 kernel launches once per grammar request and applies only the positions active in device `cu_num_logits` (e.g. bonus-only after an adaptive-verification zero-budget step).
- This removes `_build_grammar_mapping` and the worker's dependence on `cu_num_logits_np` / scheduled draft counts. Batch-sharded sampling slices whole blocks, and MRV1 unpacks blocks into its packed layout.

This replaces the CPU-side fix in #52436 (merged), so it is not a duplicate. Co-authored with #52436's author, `oops-oom`.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py \
  tests/v1/structured_output/test_structured_output_manager.py \
  tests/v1/structured_output/test_backend_guidance.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_shard.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py
# GPU: new kernel test + spec-decode cases of
# tests/entrypoints/llm/test_struct_output_generate.py on MRV1 and MRV2
```

## Test Result

- Unit tests: 102 passed, 1 xfailed. pre-commit passes.
- GPU tests: pending.

Agreed on by-req — the control flow is much clearer. I'm curious whether the old by-token mapping was meant as a copy optimization? My read is it was matching the packed variable-length mask/logit layout (one mask row ↔ one logit row) rather than saving on the copy — if anything, by-req copies less (one entry per request vs one per logit row). That 1:1 pairing is also exactly what compaction breaks.

The extra bytes, if any, come from padding short requests to fixed decode_query_len blocks, not from by-req indexing itself — a no-op on a uniform spec batch. Mixed scheduled draft lengths pay more bitmask than the packed layout, but K is small so it should be fine.

One nit: the inner for position_idx in range(MASK_STRIDE) serializes a dimension that used to live in the grid. For small stride (2–6) it's minor, but we could keep it parallel by launching grid=(num_grammar_reqs * MASK_STRIDE, ...) and recovering grammar_idx = pid // STRIDE, position_idx = pid % STRIDE — req_idx/width still come from req_indices + device cu_num_logits, and inactive positions are just cheap masked-off programs like before.
The PR should fix https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52620 as well

nodes.body:
Thanks for the work, removing the CPU-side mapping and letting the GPU logit counts decide which mask rows apply makes this path much simpler and safer. LGTM.

I tested it on live servers (H100) and compared each run with main (`153a17166e`), using the same server args and the same requests on both sides.

| What I tested | Models | Result |
|---|---|---|
| MRV1 and MRV2, xgrammar and guidance | Llama-3.1-8B + EAGLE3, Qwen3-8B + ngram | ✅ |
| Requests with fewer drafts than `k` (block only partly filled) | Qwen3-8B + ngram | ✅ |
| Adaptive verification trims some drafts on the GPU (about 35k steps) | Qwen3-4B + DSpark | ✅ |
| Adaptive verification with a zero draft budget (forced) | Qwen3-4B + DSpark | ✅ |
| Batch-sharded sampling | Llama-3.1-8B TP2 + EAGLE3, Qwen3.6-35B TP2 + MTP, Qwen3.5-122B TP4 + MTP | ✅ |
| Structured output after thinking | Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-4B, Qwen3.6-35B with `--reasoning-parser qwen3` | ✅ |

The zero-budget step did not occur on its own, even at temperature 2.0 and high load. So I forced it with a temporary patch on every 3rd step and on every step. Both runs passed, and in the every-3rd-step run, greedy outputs matched main for 96 of 96 requests.

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @LucasWilkinson.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

Agreed on by-req — the control flow is much clearer. I'm curious whether the old by-token mapping was meant as a copy optimization? My read is it was matching the packed variable-length mask/logit layout (one mask row ↔ one logit row) rather than saving on the copy — if anything, by-req copies less (one entry per request vs one per logit row). That 1:1 pairing is also exactly what compaction breaks.

The extra bytes, if any, come from padding short requests to fixed decode_query_len blocks, not from by-req indexing itself — a no-op on a uniform spec batch. Mixed scheduled draft lengths pay more bitmask than the packed layout, but K is small so it should be fine.

One nit: the inner for position_idx in range(MASK_STRIDE) serializes a dimension that used to live in the grid. For small stride (2–6) it's minor, but we could keep it parallel by launching grid=(num_grammar_reqs * MASK_STRIDE, ...) and recovering grammar_idx = pid // STRIDE, position_idx = pid % STRIDE — req_idx/width still come from req_indices + device cu_num_logits, and inactive positions are just cheap masked-off programs like before.
The PR should fix https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52620 as well

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Thanks Lucas. LGTM

ngram_gpu now works correctly with structured outputs and async scheduling

https://gist.github.com/yzong-rh/97788a6f1091348c22299c160a08d950

```
.venv/bin/vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \
  --max-model-len 768 \
  --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 768 \
  --async-scheduling \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"ngram_gpu","num_speculative_tokens":4,"prompt_lookup_min":1,"prompt_lookup_max":4}'

python spec_decode_smoke.py 
```

`19/24 requests failed` on main, `all 24 requests succeeded` with this applied.

Thanks for the work, removing the CPU-side mapping and letting the GPU logit counts decide which mask rows apply makes this path much simpler and safer. LGTM.

I tested it on live servers (H100) and compared each run with main (`153a17166e`), using the same server args and the same requests on both sides.

| What I tested | Models | Result |
|---|---|---|
| MRV1 and MRV2, xgrammar and guidance | Llama-3.1-8B + EAGLE3, Qwen3-8B + ngram | ✅ |
| Requests with fewer drafts than `k` (block only partly filled) | Qwen3-8B + ngram | ✅ |
| Adaptive verification trims some drafts on the GPU (about 35k steps) | Qwen3-4B + DSpark | ✅ |
| Adaptive verification with a zero draft budget (forced) | Qwen3-4B + DSpark | ✅ |
| Batch-sharded sampling | Llama-3.1-8B TP2 + EAGLE3, Qwen3.6-35B TP2 + MTP, Qwen3.5-122B TP4 + MTP | ✅ |
| Structured output after thinking | Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-4B, Qwen3.6-35B with `--reasoning-parser qwen3` | ✅ |

The zero-budget step did not occur on its own, even at temperature 2.0 and high load. So I forced it with a temporary patch on every 3rd step and on every step. Both runs passed, and in the every-3rd-step run, greedy outputs matched main for 96 of 96 requests.
